adjudication_label: Geometric effects on oxidation data interpretation
canonical_question: How does the difference in surface area to mass ratio between the cuboid and near half disk specimens affect the interpretation of the TGA mass gain results?

question_variants.question: How does the difference in surface area to mass ratio between the cuboid and near half disk specimens affect the interpretation of the TGA mass gain results?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The paper provides the mass and dimensions (and calculated surface area for the coated sample) for both specimen types but does not discuss the impact of the difference in surface area to mass ratio on the interpretation of the TGA results.

answers.answer: The paper lists the dimensions and masses of the cuboid (uncoated) and near half disk (silicide-coated) specimens but does not provide an analysis of how their different surface area to mass ratios affect the interpretation of the mass gain results.
answers.measurement_outcome: Mass and dimensions provided; interpretation of ratio effect not provided
evidence_spans: First, the printed samples were exposed to flowing hydrogen (99.999% pure) for de‐binding. Two steps were included in the de‐binding stage: i) evaporation of residual DCM solvent and EGBE at 150 °C for 30 min, and ii) decomposition of the PS binder polymer at 450 °C for 30 min.
Second, sintering was performed at 1400 °C, for times spanning between 15 min and 18 h, in a vacuum tube furnace with an initial vacuum level of < 3 × 10 −6 torr.
A zirconium foil was used to cover the crucible containing the samples and titanium sponges were placed in the crucible to act as an oxygen getter during sintering.

source_evidence_spans: The sintered specimens – uncoated (74 mg, cuboid, 1.8 × 2.2 × 2.1 mm) and silicide‐coated (112 mg, near half disk, R: 3.0 mm, H: 0.9 mm, surface area calculated from optical images)
